title: OAVCR Control Specification 1.1
description: Open Audio Visual Control Registry — device entry, control actions and chain slot schemas. 1.1 adds `connection` and `controls`: a device may now declare what it can be told to do, and how, so an implementation can generate a control UI without shipping per-device code.

action.description: Canonical action vocabulary. A control UI is generated from these names, so a device that calls its input switch `source_select` must still declare `input_select` — the point of the registry is that every device speaks the same nouns.

serialConnection.description: Physical/link layer for rs232 and rs485. Getting the cable wrong is the single most common integration failure, so `cable` is recorded even when the manual only implies it.

oneWay.description: IR has no return path, so an implementation cannot read state back. Defaults true.

triggerConnection.description: A 12 V trigger jack, described electrically rather than merely noted. The commonest installation failure is wiring a dry-contact relay across a trigger INPUT: a relay closes a circuit but sources no voltage, so nothing happens and the device appears faulty. Recording voltage and polarity is what lets a consumer give correct wiring guidance.

voltage.description: Nominal applied voltage, e.g. "12 V DC".

voltageRange.description: Accepted range where the maker publishes one, e.g. "3–30 V AC or DC". Tolerance varies by manufacturer and must not be assumed from another device.

polarity.description: e.g. "tip positive, sleeve ground". Use the literal "unknown" when the maker does not publish it — the same idiom as an unknown serial cable type. Saying so explicitly is a fact; leaving the field out looks like an oversight.

current.description: Current the input sinks, or that an output can source.

levelHeld.description: True when the device stays on only while the voltage is applied, as opposed to a momentary pulse that toggles it.

kind.description: `chain_device` means another device in the same signal chain supplies it — the reason a chain-aware consumer can offer a route a flat registry cannot.

examples.description: Concrete products that satisfy the requirement. Illustrative only — listing one is not an endorsement, and a registry entry must never depend on a particular vendor remaining in business.

controlOption.description: A route to controlling a device that cannot simply be talked to. Some gear ships with no data interface at all, and for those the registry's job is not to invent a command set but to state honestly what hardware or chain arrangement makes the device controllable, and what that arrangement can and cannot do.

provides.description: Actions this route makes available. Empty or absent for `manual_only`.

wiring.description: Wiring, in enough detail to be followed.

limitations.description: What this route cannot do — no state readback, no volume, and so on. Stating the ceiling prevents a consumer promising more than the route delivers.

caution.description: Anything that risks damaging equipment if got wrong. Consumers should surface this prominently, not fold it into body text.

encoding.description: How the command is put on the wire. `kind` decides which of the sibling fields carry meaning, so a consumer never has to guess how to read a value.

value.description: ascii: the literal string, with \r / \n escapes spelled out. hex: space-separated bytes. pronto: the Pronto hex burst.

address.description: IR device address, for rc5/rc6/nec/sirc. Either a `0x`-prefixed hex string or bare decimal digits — never a bare hex string, because `10` and `0x10` are different codes and a consumer cannot guess which radix was meant. Keep whichever the manufacturer published, and prefix it if they used hex.

command.description: IR command code, for rc5/rc6/nec/sirc. Same radix rule as `address`: `0x`-prefixed hex, or bare decimal.

note.description: Anything a consumer must know to use this safely — e.g. that a value is a checksum placeholder, or that a notation has not been identified yet.

param.description: An argument the action takes, e.g. the level for set_volume or the index for input_select.

label.description: Optional override for the generated UI label. Omit to use the action's default.

source.description: Citation for this encoding. Prefer an http(s) URL to the manufacturer document. Omit to inherit metadata.sources. A non-URL note is allowed only when verified is true (hardware capture).

verified.description: True only when the command has been executed against real hardware. Documented-but-untested stays false.

controlOptions.description: Routes to control this device when it has no directly usable command set. A device with an empty `controls` array and a populated `controlOptions` is a complete, useful entry — it tells an owner what to buy and how to wire it.

sources.description: Default citations for this entry. A control with no source of its own inherits the first http(s) URL here.

protocolFamily.description: Names a shared protocol so a whole range can be recognised as one driver, e.g. `jvc-dila` or `rotel-ascii-v2`.
